title: Microsoft Purview: archive SharePoint files with retention policies
summary: Hold: the site-specific PowerShell command omits the mandatory site identity, so it is not a complete command to copy into automation. The rollout, administrator opt-in, licensing, storage billing and retention behaviour are supported; smaller corrections concern citations, the risk rationale and audit-control coverage.

claims.claim: File-level archive requires a Microsoft 365 E5 licence.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining an E5 licence requirement with pay-as-you-go Archive billing.
claims.quote: File-level archive requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license. No additional setup is required to archive files by using retention policies or labels. To use the cost-saving benefits of Microsoft 365 Archive, first set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.claim: The policy creation path is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
2. Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration, and name your new retention policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an automation equivalent for configuring the Purview retention archive action.
claims.quote: Searched: New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameter retention archive files PowerShell; Purview archive retention API archive action. Opened retention-settings and both RetentionComplianceRule references; no archive-action automation found.

claims.claim: Archive billing-policy connection is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Archive > Connect a policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. ... go to the Services tab and find Microsoft 365 Archive. Select Connect a policy, turn on the Connection status toggle for the billing policy, and then select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an API or PowerShell equivalent for connecting Archive to this billing policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive connect pay-as-you-go billing policy API PowerShell enable service; Microsoft 365 Archive billing PowerShell connect. Opened archive-setup and pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node; no equivalent found. Backup application billing is a different service.

claims.claim: Archive setup requires a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.claim: The earlier Archive setup flow uses Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Settings > Org settings.
2. On the Org settings page, select Pay-as-you-go services.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an admin UI for hiding only the manual Archive action.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Archive hide manual Archive action admin center UI AllowFileArchive. Opened archive-manage and archive-faq; the documented controls are PowerShell. The archive-setup UI turns off the broader service, not just the manual action.

claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false
... This tenant setting overrides the site-level property with the same name and blocks manual file archiving across the tenant. Admin-defined policies can still archive eligible files automatically.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrators and Global Administrators can control manual file archiving.
claims.quote: SharePoint Administrators or Global Administrators can control manual file archiving for all SharePoint sites, a subset of sites, or not at all.

claims.claim: Get-SPOSite reports site-level archived file storage through ArchivedFileDiskUsed.
claims.quote: The 'ArchivedFileDiskUsed' property of the Get-SPOSite cmdlet indicates the storage consumed by all archived files on that site in bytes.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -AllowFileArchive $false is the printed command to hide manual archiving on a single site.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOSite
    [-Identity] <SpoSitePipeBind>
... -Identity ... Mandatory: | True
claims.fix: Replace `Set-SPOSite -AllowFileArchive $false` with `Set-SPOSite -Identity <site_url> -AllowFileArchive $false`, as printed at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/archive/archive-manage. The site identity is mandatory and is not supplied by the existing call.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault $false controls manual archive availability on subsequently created sites.
claims.quote: To control whether users can manually archive files on sites created in the future, use the -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault property of the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet. ... Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault $false

claims.claim: The New-RetentionComplianceRule reference lists no archive parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameter retention archive files PowerShell. Opened the full New-RetentionComplianceRule reference; read its syntax and parameters. RetentionComplianceAction lists Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete, not Archive.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-retentioncompliancerule to the page's sources to cite the reference on which this absence statement depends.

claims.claim: The Set-RetentionComplianceRule reference lists no archive parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-RetentionComplianceRule archive parameter retention archive files PowerShell. Opened the full Set-RetentionComplianceRule reference; read its syntax and parameters. RetentionComplianceAction lists Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete, not Archive.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-retentioncompliancerule to the page's sources to cite the reference on which this absence statement depends.

claims.claim: Within a retention policy or label, adding the retention archive action is what enables that policy or label to archive files.
claims.quote: Existing retention policies and labels don't archive files unless an administrator updates them to include the archive action. ... Manual file archiving doesn't need to be enabled for the archive action in retention policies or labels.

claims.claim: The medium risk rating is based on the consequences of enabling this optional control rather than exposure if it is left at its default.
claims.quote: risk: "medium"; rationale: "Nothing archives until an admin adds the archive action, but a policy then moves files out of active storage and out of Microsoft 365 Copilot indexing". The scale assigns low when nothing happens until admin opt-in.
claims.fix: Set risk to `low` and replace its rationale with: `Low. The archive action is not enabled by default, and existing retention policies do not archive files unless an administrator updates them. Leaving the new control unconfigured preserves current behaviour.`

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to search FileArchived audit records, but the controls table has no audit-monitoring row.
claims.quote: After rollout: "Search the audit log for Archived file (FileArchived) to see which policy archived what." The three table rows cover retention configuration, billing connection and the manual Archive action, not audit monitoring.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet `Search the audit log for **Archived file** (`FileArchived`) to see which policy archived what.`; its monitoring control has no corresponding row. Keep the supported audit-event description in Risk assessment.
